source_refs.note: Topic 8.2 with Fig. 8.4 (PDF 176, printed 173). Fig. 8.4 is drawn as a 3D sketch in print; the original figure shows the three paths in 2D.

blocks.text: Here are the basic types of polarization of light.
When the electric field vector oscillates in a single plane, the light is said to be linearly polarized (Fig. 8.4a). An example is light passing through a polarizing filter, as in sunglasses.

blocks.alt: Axes x and x' (horizontal), y and y' (vertical) and z and z' (drawn in perspective) meet at O. A sine wave travels along x in the x-y plane; the half-waves above the axis are filled with magenta vertical lines and those below with cyan lines. Label: Space (3D).
blocks.caption: Figure 8.4 (a): Linear polarization of light (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 8.4 (a)).

blocks.text: When the electric field rotates circularly, either clockwise (right-handed) or anticlockwise (left-handed), the light is said to be circularly polarized (Fig. 8.4b). An example is light reflected off a CD (Compact Disc) or DVD (Digital Versatile Disc).

blocks.alt: A transparent cylinder drawn in perspective round a horizontal axis arrow, with a vertical axis at its left end. Many lines of equal length run from the axis to a helix on the cylinder wall, turning steadily round the axis. Red circles of the same radius mark the path of their tips.
blocks.caption: Figure 8.4 (b): Circular polarization of light (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 8.4 (b)).

blocks.text: A combination of linear and circular polarization, in which the electric field vector traces an elliptical path, is called elliptical polarization. In elliptical polarization (Fig. 8.4c) the two components of the electric field, E_x and E_y, are not equal, and/or they differ in phase by an arbitrary angle theta. An example is light passing through a stress plate or a waveplate.

blocks.alt: A tilted ellipse centred where the x and y axes cross. Black arrows E_x along x and E_y along y start at the centre. A cyan line along the long axis is marked a, a magenta line along the short axis is marked b, and a curved arrow theta turns from the y axis to the long axis.
blocks.caption: Figure 8.4 (c): Elliptical polarization of light (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 8.4 (c)).
